restricted_key_checks.summary: A function-call key limited to publish_prediction cannot transfer, cannot call another method, cannot attach a deposit, and cannot target another account. All four were rejected by the network before any contract code ran and left the allowance unchanged.

measurements.prepaid_gas_price: A prepaid amount is priced upfront at 0.001 NEAR per Tgas (1e9 yoctoNEAR per gas) plus about 0.0009 NEAR, 10 times the 1e8 gas price the RPC reports. Probed at 100, 150, 200, 215, 230, 260 and 300 Tgas; the cost was linear. The unused part is refunded and the access-key allowance is restored, so a key allowance must exceed the largest prepaid amount even though little is spent.
measurements.net_debit_failed_publication: 0.0001835 NEAR of allowance per failed publish_prediction, the same at 100 and 60 Tgas prepaid.
measurements.net_debit_failed_keeper_call: 0.0001776 NEAR of allowance for a refused request_settlement at 30 Tgas prepaid.
measurements.settlement_prepaid_gas: request_settlement forwards 200 Tgas to the oracle, so the caller needs about 240 Tgas prepaid: 0.24 NEAR of both allowance and account balance upfront.
measurements.reference_refresh_prepaid_gas: 100 Tgas is not enough for request_price_data; outlayer.testnet failed with 'Exceeded the prepaid gas'. Use at least 250 Tgas.
measurements.storage: 442,684 bytes after deployment and initialization, 4.42684 NEAR locked.

oracle_diagnosis.reference_cache: price-oracle.testnet get_price_data for wrap.near returns price null unless a paid refresh has happened within the last 300 seconds. The last successful report on chain was recorded at 2026-11-14T13:47:05Z with multiplier 334433333 and 8 decimals, so the worker produced a price about five hours before the failed attempts.
oracle_diagnosis.outlayer_state: outlayer.testnet is not paused. Its request counter was 47539 about five minutes after our request 47516, so other accounts are using it. Whether their executions succeed is not observable without an indexer.
oracle_diagnosis.our_arguments: Both attempts sent the same input as the earlier successful diagnostics: command get_prices, tokens [wrap.near], max_age_secs 300, default resource limits. A call through request_price_data rather than oracle_call is the only difference found; both paths reach the same call_outlayer routine.
oracle_diagnosis.conclusion: No cause on our side was found. The worker reported a plain 'Failed' for the price-oracle project, version 3585b3890f49748713b43ccb9b0ef4148f317d62f4d598db80fdaffc3f3185a0. It may be transient or specific to that worker version or its upstream price source.

observations_for_scope_decisions: The oracle reference is null unless someone pays for a refresh, so every live publication needs a paid refresh first, and every settlement is a second paid worker call. A hosted service therefore needs a funded refresher with a full-access key, which cannot be a restricted key because a function-call key cannot attach a deposit.

Contract panics reach the receipt as 'WebAssembly trap: An `unreachable` opcode was executed.' with no message and no log. Interface code that matches the text of a failure (for example 'challenge window has closed') cannot work on testnet, and the runbook's expectation of 'Decision must be yes or no' from the authorization probe cannot be observed.
The public RPC https://rpc.testnet.near.org answers 429 with a deprecation warning under light use; https://test.rpc.fastnear.com worked throughout.
